title: An Indian God Just Got Invited to Comic-Con — and He's Bringing Hans Zimmer
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is eyeing San Diego Comic-Con for its full trailer debut, with a Hans Zimmer–AR Rahman concert to follow in October. Bollywood has never played this big.
body:
The same stage that has hosted the first trailers for *Avengers*, *The Batman*, and *Star Wars* is about to welcome an Indian god.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=iIyGiiGu8NM</youtube>

According to a report from **Mid-day**, producer **Namit Malhotra** and director **Nitesh Tiwari** are in advanced talks with organisers of **San Diego Comic-Con** — the world's premier pop-culture convention — to debut the first full trailer for **Ramayana: Part 1** this July. If confirmed, it would mark the first time an Indian film has claimed a Hall H-level slot at Comic-Con, a stage traditionally reserved for the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Warner Bros., and the biggest studio tentpoles on the planet.

This is not a vanity play. The team has data to back the ambition.

A focus-group screening held recently in **Los Angeles** — where Tiwari, Malhotra, and star **Ranbir Kapoor** showed early footage to a diverse international audience — reportedly received overwhelmingly positive feedback. Industry insiders say the response has convinced the producers that this isn't just a Bollywood film with VFX; it's a global event movie that can travel across cultures and languages. The footage reportedly emphasised character presence and emotional depth over large-scale action — a deliberate choice to signal that this is a prestige epic, not just a spectacle.

> "Lord Rama has been the conscience keeper of billions of people around the globe for centuries and long after. He will continue being so long after we have gone." — Ranbir Kapoor, at the LA screening

And then there's the music.

**Hans Zimmer** and **AR Rahman** — two Academy Award winners, one German, one Tamil — are collaborating on the film's score. That alone would be a headline. But the makers are reportedly planning a **live musical event in October** to showcase the soundtrack, a concert-scale spectacle designed to build momentum ahead of the Diwali release window. There are also whispers about festival screenings at major international film festivals to establish the film's prestige credentials before it goes wide.

## The Cast, the Scale, the Stakes

The ensemble is staggering. Ranbir plays **Lord Ram** — and, as he let slip during a Hollywood press interaction, **Lord Parashurama** in a dual role, a revelation that immediately sent fan theories spiralling. **Sai Pallavi** is **Sita**, a casting choice that had the internet weeping with approval. **Yash**, fresh off the *KGF* franchise, brings his brooding intensity to **Ravana**. **Sunny Deol** is **Hanuman**, and **Ravi Dubey** rounds out the divine line-up as **Lakshman**.

The VFX are being handled by **DNEG** — the same studio behind *Dune*, *Inception*, and *Tenet* — and the two-part saga reportedly clocks over **six hours** of combined runtime. Shooting for Part 2 is already 50% complete, according to Ranbir himself, with the actor noting that becoming a father to daughter Raha is what changed his mind about taking on the massive responsibility of playing Ram. Part 1 is targeting a **Diwali 2026** release, with Part 2 arriving exactly a year later.

## Why Comic-Con Changes Everything

For diaspora audiences, this moment should feel electric. Indian cinema has flirted with Hollywood recognition — *RRR* won an Oscar, *Baahubali* broke records, **SS Rajamouli** just had a permanent seat dedicated to him at the **Cinémathèque française** in Paris. But none of those films debuted their trailers at Comic-Con. None positioned themselves as direct competitors to *Spider-Man* and *The Odyssey* on the global stage.

If Ramayana pulls this off, it doesn't just signal that Indian mythological cinema has arrived. It signals that an Indian epic can sit next to a Christopher Nolan film and hold its own — not as a curiosity, but as the main event. For NRIs who grew up watching Ramanand Sagar's *Ramayan* on Doordarshan and now live minutes from an IMAX in New Jersey or Fremont, this is the version of that story they've been waiting for — one that looks like it belongs on a seventy-foot screen.

IMDb recently crowned Ramayana the **most anticipated Indian film** for the remainder of 2026, based on page views from over 250 million monthly visitors — beating out **Alpha**, **Toxic**, **King**, and **Dhamaal 4** on the list. The film is produced by **Prime Focus Studios** and **Monster Mind Creations**.

Bollywood has been building to this for years. Diwali 2026 might just be when it arrives.
